notes:
• Defeated and hidden combatants in the carousel keep a card. A defeated combatant's card had no fill at all, and a hidden one's was faded as a whole, so the map showed through both. A defeated name was lost wherever the map behind it was the same shade as the name: on the Journal's paper, dark red over a dark map, and in the dark, light red over a light one; on every device somewhere. Both keep a solid card now, on every device, and a defeated name reads whatever part of the map is behind it. A defeated one's portrait is still grayed and its name struck out, and a hidden one's portrait and name are still faded, but not the GM's buttons on it.
  • An enemy's hit points in the GM's projection, from its first hit. With an enemy's token selected, the projection showed its sheet, but the first time that enemy was hurt its hit points stayed where they were, and so did every hit after, until the token was selected again. Foundry builds an unlinked token's actor from the token, and the first change to it makes Foundry build that actor again as a new one; the projection kept drawing the old one, which is never updated. It now looks a token's actor up through the token each time it draws. Any system, and any change, not only hit points: a condition, a spent spell.
  • The private-message label on PF2e and SF2e cards with a portrait. PF2e lays such a card's header out as a grid, with a place for each part of it. The label that says who a message is for had no place there, so it was put in the narrow column under the portrait, broke onto two lines and lay over the message: on a damage-taken card with its Undo, "Only Gamemaster" covered "Wolf takes 11 damage." It now takes the place of the "To:" line it stands in for, on one line under the name.
